claims.text: Nano-scale aluminum carbide precipitates have high thermal conductivity.
Introducing nano-scale aluminum carbide precipitates into a high-entropy alloy will enhance its heat-transfer capability.
Introducing these precipitates will retain the structural integrity required of intermediate plasma-facing reactor components.
Current high-entropy-alloy intermediate layers combine balanced mechanical strength with only moderate thermal conductivity.
A controlled aluminum carbide nanoprecipitate volume fraction of approximately 5–10% is suitable for the proposed modification.
Temperatures of approximately 800–1000°C and high thermal loading are representative of plasma-reactor operating conditions relevant to the proposed intermediate layer.
Nanoprecipitate–matrix interfaces provide additional phonon-transport pathways.
The nanoprecipitate–matrix interfaces maintain grain-boundary integrity and overall microstructural stability.
Dispersed nano-scale aluminum carbide phases facilitate phonon transfer and thereby increase overall thermal conductivity.
Restricting the precipitate volume fraction to a controlled range prevents excessive embrittlement and preserves mechanical strength.
The modified alloy will exhibit moderately higher thermal conductivity than the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy will retain tensile strength under the specified high-temperature and high-loading conditions.
The modified alloy will retain fracture toughness under the specified high-temperature and high-loading conditions.
An excessively high nanoprecipitate volume fraction could offset heat-transfer gains by reducing mechanical integrity.
Precipitate coarsening during operation could offset heat-transfer gains by reducing mechanical integrity.
The predicted benefits are limited to controlled nanoprecipitate dispersions of approximately 5–10% by volume.
